fact: Senator Ned Nwoko opened a public consultation on 27 July 2026, via a Facebook post inviting internet users to give their views on bill SB.648, which would amend the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 to require large social media platforms to keep physical offices in Nigeria.
system: SB.648 (amendment of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023)

fact: After Senate examination, SB.648 went to a public hearing in Abuja organised by the Senate Committee on Information Technology and Cybersecurity, which is to study the contributions of the various stakeholders before reporting to the Senate; the document gives no date for the hearing, so its published date is used.
system: SB.648 (amendment of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023)

fact: The Senate held a public hearing on the Data Protection Bill (SB648) on 23 July 2026, which a Project Sprint-led coalition of civil society and youth organisations (Center for Africa Policy Research and Advisory, Southern Nigeria Youth Congress, Young Lawyers Forum, PCCSIGN and others) attended and supported, according to Project Sprint's country director.

The Nigerian Communications Commission, through its Joint NCC-Industry Committee, issued a consultation paper on 19 June 2026 inviting stakeholders to send written comments by 9 July 2026 on the framework for zero-rated access to educational platforms for students (structure, eligibility, funding, net neutrality, competition safeguards).
system: Zero-Rated Access to Educational Platforms framework (Zero-Rated Data Access Project)

fact: The Nigeria Data Protection Commission held validation workshops on its Data Privacy Framework for e-Commerce, a Lagos one attended by private-sector stakeholders and an Abuja one to take input from the public sector, as reported on 2026-09-11 (the document gives no workshop dates, so its publication date is used).

NITDA, through the Office for Nigerian Digital Innovation and convened by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, held a technical validation workshop in Lagos with more than 60 hub operators, startup founders and investors on the draft National Innovation Hubs Standard Framework, weeks after a stakeholders' engagement in Abuja; ThisDay reported it on 2026-09-07, which is used as the date because the document says only 'recently'.

The Nigeria Data Protection Commission held validation workshops on a Data Privacy Framework for e-commerce, an earlier one in Lagos with private-sector stakeholders and one in Abuja with ministries, departments, agencies and other stakeholders, as reported on 3 September 2026 (no event date given, so the published date is used).

The Nigerian Communications Commission held its first public consultation forum in Abuja on the proposed framework for zero-rated access to educational platforms and content, with the telecom operators' association ALTON, UNESCO, uLesson Group and the Nigerian Governors' Forum among those present; the date 14 July 2026 comes from the source's ingest note, the article saying only Tuesday.
system: Zero-Rated Access to Educational Platforms and Content in Nigeria framework

fact: The OGP Independent Reporting Mechanism reports that Nigeria's Open Government Partnership action plan 2023-2025, which includes the open contracting portal NOCOPO, was co-created through a government and civil society steering committee with online surveys, public notices, town halls and validation meetings, and that citizen input shaped priorities including digital platforms; the document gives no date for the co-creation, so its publication date 2026-04-28 is used.

The National Assembly held a public hearing on 10 November 2025 on the National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill 2024, at which the Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria presented a position paper to the Joint National Assembly Committee on ICT, Cybersecurity, and Digital Economy.

fact: The Senate and House joint committees held a one-day public hearing on the National Digital Economy and e-Governance Bill 2025 with public and private sector stakeholders, and the Ministry says the bill was presented to stakeholders in all 36 states and the FCT.
